main_text.p: paulatim profecerūt in cognitione Christi: utipsimet fatentur. Paulus autem [?] Christo, eodem fere momento, didicit Evangelium per miràdam reuelationem: quòd ita ei opus esset.

Nos, cum necesse sit legendo sacras literas, & exercitijs veræ pietatis & tolerantiæ, Dei dona suscitare, per gradus [illegible, ~6 letters] proficimus. Vtinam autem, quantū quidem in nobis est, demus operam, ut profectus noster aliquando manifestus sit in omnibus: & ut dissimilimi simus illis mulierculis, quas semper discere, nunquam autem ad veritatis cognitionem peruenire, Apostolus noster queritur.
3. Obiectorum respectu distingui potest ignorantia, in Rerum & Personarum, Factorum & Iuris ignorantiam.
I. Rerum aliæ nobis notæ esse debent, aliæ contra ignotæ.

Rectè Aristoteles in Rhetoricis: Turpe, inquit, est ignorare, quod universos scire convenit. Vt Dei sanctam voluntatem nos omnes scire & præstare decet: cum ideò simus conditi, ut Deum agnoscamus, & ei obediamus. Idem iudicium est & de uniuscuiusque officio in socie-

page.notes: Running head "HYPOMNEMATA" and the page number 194 are read from the scan; the page number is clear enough but the old-style figures are slightly blurred. The Greek word after "per gradus" is not legible on the scan, and a second Greek word above it is also unreadable; both are replaced by the placeholder. The word "autem" is followed by a small mark that is unclear; it is marked [?] and may be a printer's sign. "Paulus" is printed with a shape close to "Panlus" and is read as Paulus. Final word "socie-" is split at the line end, with the catchword "tatę" completing it below. Possible printing features retained as printed: "ideò", "præstare", "Rectè".
